record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.context_brief: L-group orbits on the stable class
record.original_question: Let M be a closed connected compact 2q-manifold, let pi = pi1(M), let w1 be its orientation character, and let S_st(M) be the stable class of M: diffeomorphism classes of 2q-manifolds with the same Euler characteristic as M that become diffeomorphic to M after connected sum with some W_g = #g(S^q x S^q). The surgery L-group L_{2q+1}(Z[pi], w1) acts on S_st(M) by Wall realisation. Determine the orbit set S_st(M) / L_{2q+1}(Z[pi], w1).

evidence.quote: Recall that pi = pi1(M) and w1 = w1(M) are the fundamental group and orientation character of M and that the L-group L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) acts on the stable class of M via Wall realisation
Problem. Determine Sst(M)/L2q+1(Z[pi],w1), the set of orbits of the action of L2q+1(Z[pi],w1) on the stable class.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed connected compact smooth $2q$-manifold. Denote by $\pi = \pi_1(M)$ its fundamental group and by $w_1 = w_1(M)\colon \pi \to \{\pm 1\}$ its orientation character. For each integer $g \ge 0$ set $W_g := \#_g (S^q \times S^q)$, the $g$-fold connected sum.

Define the stable class of $M$ to be
$$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{st}}(M) := \{[N] : N \text{ is a closed } 2q\text{-manifold with } \chi(N)=\chi(M) \text{ and } N \# W_g \cong M \# W_g \text{ for some } g \ge 0\},$$
where $[N]$ denotes the diffeomorphism class of $N$.

Let $L_{2q+1}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi], w_1)$ denote the Wall surgery $L$-group of the group ring $\mathbb{Z}[\pi]$ with involution twisted by $w_1$. Via Wall realisation, $L_{2q+1}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi], w_1)$ acts on $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{st}}(M)$.

Problem. Compute, in terms of the homotopy/algebraic invariants of $(M, \pi, w_1)$, the orbit set
$$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{st}}(M) \big/ L_{2q+1}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi], w_1).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on the topology of manifolds. Web searches reveal no general solution; existing work (Kreck's modified surgery, results on homotopy stable classes for highly connected manifolds) treats only special cases, suggesting the general orbit-set computation remains open.
